exact_checked_claims.claim: For fixed n >= 3 nontrivial finitely generated factors, fixed finite nonempty inverse-closed generating sets of nonidentity elements and fixed 1/3 < d < 1, the rooted exact-length cyclic syllable quotient with floor(|S_ell|^d) independent uniform samples with replacement has property (T) with probability tending to one through all integer lengths.

The complete multipartite alphabet matrix has one positive eigenvalue, all other normalized eigenvalues in [-rho,0] for fixed rho < 1, and inverse-fixed block deletion is exponentially negligible in every endpoint class.
Retained non-inverse-fixed blocks form valid formal inverse pairs and cyclically reduced triangular relations; the corresponding group maps onto the block subgroup of the original quotient.
For L >= 4 the subgroup generated by V_L contains every two-letter product and has index at most two, using explicit suffixes that remain valid with torsion.

The expected link entry is (N_ell/Z_ell)c_tu A_ac T_(ell-t-u)(b,f), with C_0=[6], C_1=[[2,2],[2,0]], C_2=[[0,2],[2,2]]. The identity uses rooted fixed-position corner counts and includes all rejection events.

Fixed-dimensional endpoint compression converges to Q tensor P tensor R. The unequal type eigenvalue -1/2 times the negative spectrum of P gives maximal nonprincipal eigenvalue rho/2 < 1/2, yielding eventual mean gap gamma=(3-rho)/4.

Independent whole-relator PSD Laplacians have norm at most six; after expected-degree normalization and restriction to the deterministic common-kernel complement, the lower-tail exponent is epsilon^2 gamma delta_ell/12. Degree contributions are at most three, giving upper-tail exponent epsilon^2 delta_ell/9.

Generalized Courant–Fischer on the expected-degree-centered codimension-one subspace yields actual link gap at least (1-epsilon)gamma/(1+epsilon)>1/2, without identifying actual and expected orthogonality.

The independent uniform linear-normal-word law has the same property (T) conclusion via binomial thinning to a prescribed number of cyclic words at a smaller density d-prime strictly between 1/3 and d.

verdict.followup_rationale: No new public follow-up is proposed. Two-factor even-length laws, the critical density and lower density thresholds are substantial pre-existing or natural directions, but this review has not established a new mechanism or a sufficiently supported conjecture for them. Listing them merely as extensions would not meet the requested high bar.
key_boundaries: The result requires at least three factors. It does not resolve the full two-factor version of Question 1.9 in Random Quotients of Free Products; for two factors the odd-length cyclic universe is empty.

There is no conclusion at d = 1/3, no finite-length guarantee, and no uniform estimate when the factors, alphabet sizes, ball radius or density vary with relator length. The one-third bound is sufficient, not claimed sharp.

The law is uniform sampling with replacement from rooted cyclically reduced syllable words of exact length. It must not be silently replaced by uniform conjugacy classes, ordinary free-group words, a different word metric, or sampling without replacement.

The theorem proves property (T), not infinitude or factor embeddings. Above one-half, known collapse already implies property (T); those facts and the models to which they apply require their own hypotheses.

The three-block spectral strategy, almost-equal blocks, common-suffix finite-index method, link criterion and matrix concentration have explicit predecessors. The contribution is their model-specific completion. No exhaustive novelty, historical firstness or universal Gromov-model threshold is claimed.
The finite verification routines test exact formulas and artifact integrity. They cannot certify the asymptotic theorem, property (T), external proof dependencies or priority.
